user.text:
The public library bills overdue fees once a month from the circulation exports of its branches, in /app/data. Write a Python script at /app/bin/fees.py that turns the exports and the lending files into the fee statements by the rules in /app/docs (start with /app/docs/overview.md) and writes the statements file described in /app/docs/output.md. It is run as `python3 /app/bin/fees.py INPUT_DIR OUTPUT_FILE`. Run it on /app/data and save the result as /app/out/statements.json.

From /app, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` runs the script on a few small inputs, and `python tools/check_fees.py` compares /app/out/statements.json with the approved statements for the current period. The script will also be run on the exports and lending files of other periods, with other branches, patrons and calendars, so it must follow the documented rules rather than what the current files happen to contain. Use only the Python standard library. Do not change anything under /app/data, /app/docs, /app/tests or /app/tools.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

# Overdue fee statements: overview

The library lends books, DVDs, magazines, laptops and kits from its
branches. Once a month the fee run reads the circulation exports of every
branch together with the lending policy, and writes one fee statement per
patron with overdue loans and a summary per branch. This note says what goes
in, what comes out and in which order the work is done. The rules for each
step live in their own notes:

| Note | Covers |
|---|---|
| `lending.md` | the lending files: policy, branches, calendar, patrons, waivers |
| `exports.md` | the circulation export files and their events, local times, voids |
| `loans.md` | how events become loans: due dates, renewals, returns, the period |
| `fees.md` | overdue days, grace, the fee of a loan, waivers, the statement cap |
| `output.md` | the statements file |
| `changelog.md` | what changed between versions of these rules |

Where this note and a numbered rule in another note seem to disagree, the
numbered rule wins. The rules apply to every run the same way: nothing in
them depends on a particular branch, patron, item or month.

## 1. Inputs

1.1 An input directory holds `policy.ini`, `branches.csv`, `calendar.csv`,
`patrons.csv` and `waivers.csv` (`lending.md`), and a directory `exports/`
with the export files of the branches (`exports.md`).

1.2 The exports are raw: they overlap, they repeat events, they hold events
that were cancelled later, and they run a few days past the end of the
statement period. `exports.md` and `loans.md` say which events

## 1. policy.ini

1.1 `policy.ini` is an INI file: sections in square brackets, one
`key = value` per line, and comment lines that start with `#`. Values have no
quotes. Amounts of money are written in currency units with two decimals
(`0.25`) and stand for whole cents (25).

1.2 Section `[statement]`: `library` (the library's name), `period_start` and
`period_end` (dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, both included in the period).

1.3 Section `[clock]`: the library's offset from UTC.

- `offset` is the offset in force before the first change, written `-06:00`.
- `changes` lists the changes, separated by `;`, in time order. Each change
  is an instant in UTC written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ`, a space and the offset in
  force from that instant on. `changes` can be empty.

1.4 One section `[item:TYPE]` per item type (`[item:book]`, `[item:dvd]`):

- `loan_days`: days from a checkout or a counted renewal to the due date
  (`loans.md` 2 and 3);
- `renewals`: the most renewals of one loan that count (`loans.md` 3.1);
- `grace_days`: the grace allowance (`fees.md` 1.2);
- `daily`: the fee per charged day;
- `loan_cap`: the most that one loan of this type is assessed before a
  discount (`fees.md` 2.3).

1.5 One section `[category:NAME]` per patron category:

- `statement_cap`: the most that one statement of a patron of this category
  bills (`fees.md` 4), or `none` for no cap;
- `discount`: a whole percentage taken off the fee of each loan (`fees.md`
  2.4), 0 for none;
- `exempt`: item types, separated by commas, whose loans this category is
  never charged for (`fees.md` 2.2); it can be empty.

Item types and category names are compared without regard to case.

## 2. branches.csv

2.1 Columns `branch`, `name`, `open_days`. `open_days` lists the weekdays on
which the branch opens, as three-letter English names separated by spaces
(`Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat`).

2.2 The order of the rows is the order of the branch summary (`output.md`
4.1).

## 3. calendar.csv

3.1 Columns `date`, `branch`, `status`, `note`. The note carries nothing for
the fee run.

3.2 `date` is one day (`2027-02-15`) or a range of days `FIRST..LAST`
(`2027-01-28..2027-02-04`), both days included.

3.3 `branch` is a branch id, or `*` for every branch.

3.4 `status` is `closed` or `open`. An `open` row opens the branch on a day it
would otherwise be closed: a holiday, or a weekday that is not in its
`open_days`.

3.5 Whether a branch is open on a day:

- if a row naming that branch covers the day, its status decides;
- otherwise, if a `*` row covers the day, its status decides;
- otherwise the branch is open when the weekday is in its `open_days`.

Two rows of the same kind (one branch, or `*`) never cover the same day.

## 4. patrons.csv

4.1 Columns `patron`, `category`, `since`, `home_branch`. A patron has one
row per category they have held; `since` is the first day of that category.

4.2 The category of a patron on a day is the category of their row with the
latest `since` on or before that day.

## 5. Patron numbers

5.1 Exports and waivers write the patron number in several ways: with or
without the letter `P` in either case, with or without a hyphen or a space
after it, with or without leading zeros. `P-981`, `p981`, `P000981`,
`0000981`, `p-000981` and `P 981` are the same patron. Two patron numbers are
the same patron when their digits give the same number.

5.2 Statements name the patron as `patrons.csv` writes the number.

## 6. waivers.csv

6.1 Columns `waiver`, `patron`, `loan`, `value`, `status`.

- `loan` is a loan id, or `*` for every loan of the patron's

All amounts are whole cents. `policy.ini` values are those of the item type
of the loan and of the patron's category named in each rule.

## 1. Overdue days

1.1 The overdue days of a loan are the days after its due date, up to and
including its end day, on which the checkout branch is open (`lending.md`
3.5). The end day is the return date, or `period_end` for a loan still out at
the end of the period (`loans.md` 5.1). Days on which the checkout branch is
closed are never overdue days, whatever branch the item is returned to.

1.2 Grace allowance, by `grace_days` of the item type:

- A loan with no more overdue days than `grace_days` is charged for none of them.
- A loan with more overdue days than `grace_days` is charged for every one of its overdue days, the first ones included.

1.3 The charged days of a loan are the overdue days it is charged for.

## 2. The assessed fee of a loan

2.1 The base fee is the charged days times `daily`.

2.2 When the item type is listed in `exempt` of the patron's category on the
checkout date, the base fee is 0.

2.3 The base fee is cut to `loan_cap` when it is higher.

2.4 The discount of the patron's category on the checkout date is taken off
the result of 2.3: the assessed fee is that amount times (100 minus
`discount`) divided by 100, rounded to a whole cent, with half a cent
rounded up. With a discount of 50, 125 cents give 63.

## 3. Waivers

3.1 A waiver applies to a loan of a statement when it is active, its patron
is the patron of the loan (`lending.md` 5), and its `loan` is the loan id or
`*`.

3.2 When a waiver that applies is `full`, the waived amount is the assessed
fee. Otherwise the waived amount is the sum of the amounts of the waivers that
apply, but never more than the assessed fee. A `*` waiver with an amount
applies that amount to each loan of the statement.

3.3 The net fee of a loan is its assessed fee minus its waived amount.

## 4. The statement cap

4.1 The statement cap is `statement_cap` of the patron's category on
`period_end`. With `none` there is no cap.

4.2 When the net fees of the loans of a statement add up to more than the
cap, the excess is capped. It is taken from the loans in order of due date,
latest first, and for loans with the same due date, from the loan id that
sorts last as text first. Each loan gives up as much of its net fee as the
excess still needs, and no more than its net fee.

4.3 The billed fee of a loan is its net fee minus what it gave up to the cap.

## 5. Which loans are on a statement

5.1 A statement lists every loan of the patron that is part of the run
(`loans.md` 5.2) and has at least one overdue day, including loans charged
nothing because of grace, an exemption or a waiver.

5.2 A patron with no such loan gets no statement.
